name: Briar Corona
classification: Self-Sustaining Plasma Maelstrom / Class-IX Energetic Hazard

detectability.signature: Intense broadband electromagnetic emission across all frequencies, with characteristic thorned discharge pattern on magnetometric scans

proximity: Progressive electromagnetic interference beginning at 0.5 AU, rendering unshielded communications and sensors inoperable
Hull temperature rises measurably from radiant energy absorption
Charged particle bombardment causes visible Saint Elmo's fire across all external surfaces
contact: Immediate and total failure of unshielded electronic systems
Plasma arcs strike the hull with energies sufficient to ablate standard armor plating
Radiation exposure reaches lethal thresholds within minutes for unprotected crew
prolonged_exposure: Complete structural failure as plasma erosion breaches even military-grade hull composites
Catastrophic radiation saturation of all internal spaces
Ship reduced to molten debris within hours

age: Approximately 12,000 years, seeded by a stellar collision event whose remnants are still visible at the storm's core

behavior.cycle: Major discharge events every 8 to 22 hours, with continuous low-level plasma activity between pulses

phenomena: Plasma tendrils extend from the main body in branching, thorn-like formations that reach out and retract over hours
The storm's core contains a sustained fusion reaction feeding on interstellar hydrogen swept up by its own magnetic fields
Periodic mega-discharges produce electromagnetic pulses detectable across neighboring star systems
The storm generates its own localized magnetic field strong enough to deflect solar winds from nearby stars
hazards: Plasma tendrils can extend unpredictably up to 0.4 AU beyond the storm's apparent boundary, striking without warning
Electromagnetic pulse events can disable ships well outside the visible storm radius
The storm's gravitational influence from compressed plasma mass creates navigational hazards in surrounding space
opportunities: The sustained fusion core represents an effectively inexhaustible energy source if harvesting technology can be developed
Plasma composition includes heavy elements forged in the original stellar collision, available nowhere else in such concentrations
The storm's magnetic field dynamics offer a natural laboratory for studying magnetohydrodynamics at extreme scales
known_incidents: The heavy cruiser Thistledown approached within 0.3 AU on a survey mission in 2419 with military-grade shielding. It survived forty minutes before an unpredicted tendril discharge forced emergency withdrawal, losing two engine nacelles and sustaining sixty percent hull ablation.

An autonomous harvesting drone deployed by the Helix Energy Consortium in 2461 successfully extracted seventeen tons of heavy-element plasma before being destroyed by a mega-discharge, proving the commercial viability of storm-harvesting but also its extraordinary risk.
description: The Briar Corona is a catastrophic beauty visible from light-years away, a seething elliptical maelstrom of superheated plasma that writhes and branches like an enormous thornbush made of captive starfire. Its dominant colors shift between blinding white at the core and deep arterial red at its thorned extremities, with veins of electric blue tracing the magnetic field lines that give the storm its structure. The entire formation spans over six AU across its long axis and radiates enough energy to be mistaken for a small star on long-range sensors.

The storm is in constant violent motion, its plasma tendrils extending and retracting in patterns that defy prediction. Major discharge events occur irregularly, sending arcs of stellar-temperature plasma lashing outward in thorned whips that can span hundreds of thousands of kilometers in seconds. Between these events, the storm churns with a lower but still lethal intensity, its magnetic field lines snapping and reconnecting in cascades that produce continuous radiation across the entire electromagnetic spectrum.

Born from the collision of two stellar remnants twelve millennia ago, the Briar Corona should have dissipated within centuries. Instead, its magnetic architecture trapped sufficient hydrogen to sustain an ongoing fusion reaction at its core, creating a self-feeding engine of destruction that has only grown more powerful over time. It has consumed at least three known cometary bodies and an unknown quantity of interstellar gas, each addition fueling further growth. The original collision remnants are still faintly detectable at the storm's heart, locked in an eternal embrace of mutual annihilation.

The Briar Corona is currently in what astrophysicists term an active accretion phase, with its outer boundary expanding at a measurable rate as it sweeps up surrounding material. Mega-discharge frequency has increased over the past century, and the storm's overall energy output has risen by an estimated eleven percent in the last decade alone. Long-range hazard beacons maintain a two-AU exclusion zone, though the unpredictable reach of plasma tendrils has prompted calls to extend this to three AU. Several parties continue to express interest in energy harvesting despite the extreme risks, driven by the staggering value of the storm's heavy-element plasma.
